kill_argument: H1 is still a confirmatory test with a 0.005 margin on an instrument whose noise floor is two to eight times that margin; the design-r1 fix makes the claim honest rather than informative. Scoped to 'the plug-in 15-bin estimator on these samples', H1 can come out supported or contradicted purely from how RF and LR spread predictions across equal-mass bins (a sharper, well-calibrated RF has a lower floor and reads as better calibrated), yet the contribution still sells it as 'a replication of a known calibration result'. A referee would say the verdict either replicates Niculescu-Mizil and Caruana or measures an estimator artefact, and the paper cannot tell which without a heuristic sensitivity it has promised never to let decide. What held: plan.json sha256 a697fbf6... matches the last designer log line; method step 8's ece_db matches Kumar et al. arXiv v2 Def. G.3 and its 'heuristic' caveat; draw seeds are fixed; the amendment is disclosed before any run; runs/ holds only data-prep runs; validate is OK. Because the claim is now scoped and the disagreement rule pre-stated, this is minor, not major.

findings.text: The contribution and H1's label still call H1 'a replication of a known calibration result' (Niculescu-Mizil and Caruana 2005), but after the F1 amendment the H1 verdict is explicitly a statement about the plug-in 15-bin equal-mass estimator on these samples, which can be decided by the difference of noise floors (H1 text: 'if both are well calibrated, it equals the difference of their floors, whose sign depends on how each model spreads its predictions'). A 'supported' or 'contradicted' H1 therefore does not by itself replicate or fail to replicate a claim about calibration. The wording invites exactly the overreach the amendment was meant to prevent, and it will propagate into the abstract. Resolving evidence (no experiment needed): reword the contribution and the H1 label to say H1 tests, on the plug-in estimator, the direction Niculescu-Mizil and Caruana reported, and commit that the paper will call H1 a replication only where the ece_db sensitivity agrees in direction.
findings.evidence: plan.json contribution ('a replication of a known calibration result (H1)'); plan.json hypotheses[0] opening '(replication; Niculescu-Mizil and Caruana 2005)' versus the same entry's scope sentence; design.threats[0] last sentence
findings.response: PI: H1 label and contribution reworded to a test of the published direction on the plug-in estimator, 'replication' only where the debiased ECE agrees; disclosed as a post-question-gate amendment.
